title: 🍽️ Culinary Empire
theme: Build a thriving restaurant from your cooking competition win
description: You've won a local cooking competition and earned 500 Mento Coins! The prize includes the opportunity to open a small restaurant space for the summer. Your food is delicious, but can you run a successful restaurant? Master ingredients, staffing, customer service, and finances while competing with other restaurants in town!

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read each restaurant management scenario and decide how to handle it
Make choices about menu items, staffing, pricing, and customer service
Watch how decisions affect your Restaurant Rating, Food Quality, and Mento Coins
Manage both staff and ingredients -- great food needs both skilled cooks and quality supplies
Grow from a small eatery to a culinary empire by maximizing Happy Diners and weekly revenue
tips: Balance Food Quality and Service Quality -- both matter for your Restaurant Rating
Hiring more staff costs money but improves service during busy periods
Keep an eye on your weekly revenue vs. expenses to avoid going bankrupt

learning_objectives: Manage the operational complexity of running a restaurant including menu design, ingredient sourcing, staffing, and customer service
Balance food quality and service quality to build a strong restaurant rating and earn repeat customers
Make strategic hiring and staffing decisions that affect both costs and service capacity during peak hours
Practice financial management by tracking weekly revenue versus expenses, controlling food costs, and avoiding bankruptcy
Respond to competitive pressures and unexpected events like food critics, health inspections, and supply chain disruptions

rounds.title: Round 1: Restaurant Concept
rounds.story:
Congratulations on winning the cooking competition! You have {{mento_coins}} Mento Coins and a restaurant space for summer.

Before opening, you need to decide your CONCEPT. This determines everything:
• Your menu type
• Your target customers  
• Your costs and pricing
• Your competitive positioning

Choose wisely - your concept is your brand identity!
rounds.goal: Define your restaurant concept and market positioning

choices.label: Fast Casual Healthy Bowls
choices.description: Quick service, fresh ingredients, health-conscious crowd. Customizable grain bowls with fresh vegetables and proteins. Moderate costs, good margins, appeals to fitness-minded customers.
choices.feedback: Healthy bowls chosen! Perfect timing - wellness trend is strong. You'll offer customizable grain bowls with organic ingredients. Health-conscious crowd will appreciate this!
choices.narrative_outcome: Your concept is modern, Instagram-worthy, and appeals to young professionals and fitness enthusiasts. Your menu design emphasizes nutrition and freshness.

choices.label: Fusion Fine Dining
choices.description: Upscale creative menu blending cultures. Japanese-Italian fusion with molecular gastronomy. Higher prices, sophisticated customers. High costs, premium positioning. Ambitious!
choices.feedback: Fine dining fusion! Bold and ambitious. Japanese-Italian with molecular touches. If you execute well, you'll be the talk of the town. High risk, high reward!
choices.narrative_outcome: You're creating something unique - miso carbonara, sake-braised short ribs, yuzu tiramisu. Critics will notice. Can you deliver on this ambitious vision?

choices.label: Comfort Food Diner
choices.description: Classic American comfort food. Mac and cheese, burgers, chicken pot pie. Familiar menu, broad appeal. Lower margins but high volume potential. Safe bet.
choices.feedback: Comfort food classics! Mac and cheese, burgers, homemade pies. Everyone loves comfort food. Safe, familiar, consistently profitable approach.
choices.narrative_outcome: You're betting on nostalgia and quality execution. Your grandma's recipes meet modern presentation. Broad appeal across age groups.

choices.label: Experimental Pop-Up Kitchen
choices.description: Menu changes weekly based on seasonal ingredients! Creative freedom, food enthusiast target. Unpredictable but exciting. Requires constant innovation.
choices.feedback: Rotating concept! Every week is different based on what's fresh and inspiring. Food bloggers are intrigued. This is culinary adventure!
choices.narrative_outcome: You'll need constant creativity and flexibility. This week: farm-to-table vegetarian. Next week: seafood showcase. Keeps you and customers excited!

rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant restaurant space filled with colorful decor, tables set with cheerful tableware, a large chalkboard displaying menu ideas, sunlight streaming through large windows
rounds.coaching_moment: Consider how this choice affects your long-term resources, not just the immediate gain.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What tradeoff did this decision reveal? What did you gain, and what did you give up?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 2: Menu Pricing Strategy
rounds.story:
Your restaurant concept is set! Food quality: {{food_quality}}/100

Now the critical decision: PRICING STRATEGY

You need to calculate:
• Food cost per dish (ingredients)
• Labor cost (staff time)
• Overhead (rent, utilities)
• Desired profit margin

Most restaurants aim for 25-35% food cost. How will you price?

choices.label: Cost-Plus Standard (30% food cost)
choices.description: Traditional restaurant math: Calculate food cost, add 30% markup. Industry standard, safe, proven. If a dish costs 10 MC in ingredients, charge 14 MC.
choices.feedback: Standard pricing adopted! You calculate every dish's food cost and maintain healthy 30% ratio. Predictable, proven approach.

choices.label: Value Pricing (attract volume)
choices.description: Price below competitors to pack the restaurant. Lower margins but hope to make it up in volume. Risky if volume doesn't materialize.
choices.feedback: Aggressive value pricing! Your prices are 15-20% below competitors. Tables are full but you need HIGH volume to profit.

choices.label: Premium Positioning (50% markup)
choices.description: Price high to signal quality and exclusivity. Smaller customer base but much higher margins. Must deliver exceptional quality to justify prices.
choices.feedback: Premium pricing! You're 30-40% above market. Atmosphere, service, and food MUST be impeccable. You're competing on quality, not price.

choices.label: Dynamic Menu Pricing
choices.description: Prices vary based on ingredient costs, day of week, and demand. Complex but optimized. Lunch specials, happy hours, surge pricing on weekends.
choices.feedback: Sophisticated dynamic pricing! Fish prices up? Adjust immediately. Monday lunch special at 2pm to fill slow hours. Data-driven approach!

rounds.image_prompt: a bustling restaurant kitchen filled with vibrant ingredients, chefs skillfully preparing dishes, charts and calculations on a nearby table, warm lighting creating a lively atmosphere
rounds.coaching_moment: Think about trade-offs: what are you giving up to get this benefit?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

rounds.title: Round 3: Staffing Decision
rounds.story:
You can't run a restaurant alone! Current funds: {{mento_coins}} MC

Staffing is one of the biggest expenses:
• Labor typically 25-35% of revenue
• More staff = better service but higher costs
• Too few staff = overwhelmed, poor service

How will you staff your restaurant?
rounds.goal: Balance labor costs with service quality

choices.label: Minimal Staff (You + 2 part-timers)
choices.description: Keep labor costs low. You handle most work yourself. 100 MC/week. Exhausting but profitable if you can sustain the pace.
choices.feedback: Lean team! You're doing everything - cooking, serving, cleaning. Costs are low but you're exhausted. Can you sustain this?

choices.label: Balanced Team (You + chef + 3 servers)
choices.description: Professional setup with proper front and back of house. 250 MC/week. Quality service, you can focus on management. Sustainable approach.
choices.feedback: Solid team built! Talented chef handles kitchen while you manage front of house. Servers provide good service. This is sustainable!

choices.label: Premium Team (experienced professionals)
choices.description: Hire experienced chef from fine dining, professional servers. 400 MC/week. Exceptional quality but highest costs. Best service possible.
choices.feedback: Top talent recruited! Chef from Michelin-starred restaurant, experienced servers, professional management. Expensive but quality is undeniable!

choices.label: Family & Friends Partnership
choices.description: Work with trusted people, split profits instead of wages. 0 MC upfront but they get 30% of profits. Strong chemistry but mixes business with personal.
choices.feedback: Family business! Friends and family work alongside you. No upfront costs but they share in profits. Trust and chemistry are there!

rounds.image_prompt: a bustling restaurant interior with colorful decor, busy tables filled with diners, a cheerful server taking orders, and a chalkboard displaying daily specials, warm lighting creating a lively atmosphere
rounds.coaching_moment: How might your team react to this decision? What about your customers?
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why did you choose this option? What were you trying to protect or grow?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 4: Supply Chain Disaster
rounds.story:
CRISIS! It's Friday night - busiest time of the week. You're fully booked: {{happy_diners}} reservations!

Then your main supplier calls: Truck broke down. Half your ingredients won't arrive until tomorrow morning.

You have 3 hours until service starts. Customers are counting on you. What do you do?
rounds.goal: Handle unexpected supply crisis under pressure
rounds.setting: Restaurant kitchen - 3 hours before busy service

choices.label: Emergency Grocery Store Run
choices.description: Buy ingredients from local supermarkets at retail prices. Expensive (150 MC) but you can open. Margins crushed but customers served.
choices.feedback: You sprint to three stores buying everything available! Costs way more than normal but you're open. Customers don't know anything was wrong!

choices.label: Create Limited 'Chef's Selection' Menu
choices.description: Make special tasting menu with only available ingredients. Turn constraint into exclusive feature. Creative problem-solving!
choices.feedback: Brilliant! You announce special 'Farm to Table' limited menu. Some customers are MORE excited about exclusive, curated experience!

choices.label: Cancel Tonight, Full Refunds
choices.description: Close tonight, give refunds, apologize profusely. Protects reputation long-term but loses revenue and disappoints people tonight.
choices.feedback: Hard decision to close. Customers disappointed but you're honest about situation and provide refunds. Standards matter more than money tonight.

choices.label: Call Competitor Restaurant for Help
choices.description: Swallow pride, call nearby restaurant, borrow ingredients. Promise to return favor. Build industry relationships through vulnerability.
choices.feedback: You call Mama's Diner - they help! Industry solidarity. You serve customers AND built valuable relationship. Sometimes competitors can be allies!

rounds.image_prompt: a bustling restaurant kitchen filled with chefs in action, pots steaming, frantic energy as they strategize around a large table cluttered with missing ingredient lists and notes
rounds.coaching_moment: Look at your current resource levels — which constraint are you trying to address?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 5: The Food Critic
rounds.story:
SURPRISE! A food blogger with 500K followers just walked in unannounced.

Your reputation: {{reputation}}/100
Food quality: {{food_quality}}/100
Service quality: {{service_quality}}/100

Your host recognizes them. This review could make or break you! They're being seated RIGHT NOW.

How do you handle this high-pressure moment?

choices.label: Treat Like Any Other Customer
choices.description: Don't change anything. Give them same experience everyone gets. Authentic and fair. If your restaurant is good, it's good for everyone.
choices.feedback: You treat them normally. Critic appreciates that you didn't fuss or change your service. Authenticity shines through!

choices.label: Send Complimentary Dishes
choices.description: Give extra attention, send best dishes complimentary. Strategic showcase but potentially obvious. They might see through it.
choices.feedback: You send signature dishes with complimentary amuse-bouche. Critic notices the attention but food speaks for itself. Sometimes you take your shot!

choices.label: Introduce Yourself Openly
choices.description: Walk over, acknowledge you know who they are, ask for honest feedback. Bold, transparent, confident leadership approach.
choices.feedback: You introduce yourself directly. 'I know who you are. I'm new, learning, and would appreciate honest feedback.' They're impressed by confidence and transparency!

choices.label: Don't Acknowledge, Perfect Everything
choices.description: Pretend you don't know but ensure EVERYTHING is flawless. Silent excellence. Let food and service earn the review.
choices.feedback: You act normal but ensure perfection. Every detail matters tonight. Critic enjoys meal without feeling special treatment. Your quality earns the review!

rounds.image_prompt: a bustling restaurant interior filled with vibrant decor, a surprised waiter setting a table for a well-known food blogger, warm overhead lights casting a cozy glow
rounds.coaching_moment: Sometimes the bold choice carries risk, but also the highest reward. Weigh carefully.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How might the people affected by this choice experience the outcome?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

rounds.title: Round 6: Growth Opportunity
rounds.story:
Three months in - you're profitable!

Current status:
• Funds: {{mento_coins}} MC
• Reputation: {{reputation}}/100
• Happy Diners: {{happy_diners}}
• Weekly Revenue: {{weekly_revenue}} MC

Three expansion opportunities present themselves. You can pursue ONE.

Which growth path do you choose?

choices.label: Open Second Location (350 MC)
choices.description: Replicate success in nearby town. Double your presence. Requires training new staff, maintaining quality across locations. Empire building!
choices.feedback: Location #2 opening! You're building a restaurant empire. Challenge: maintaining quality and culture across multiple sites!

choices.label: Launch Catering Service (200 MC)
choices.description: New revenue stream! Weddings, corporate events, parties. Uses existing kitchen and team. Different business model but diversifies income.
choices.feedback: Catering division launched! Weddings, corporate events, parties. Different from restaurant service but leverages your kitchen and reputation!

choices.label: Add Chef's Table Tasting Menu (180 MC)
choices.description: Exclusive 8-seat experience with multi-course tasting menu. Same location but premium offering. Higher margins, elevates entire brand.
choices.feedback: Chef's Table created! Intimate 8-seat experience with wine pairing. Exclusive, expensive, brand-elevating. You're moving upmarket!

choices.label: Bottle Signature Sauces (250 MC)
choices.description: Retail product line! Your sauces in stores. Brand extension, passive income, wider exposure. Takes time but builds lasting brand.
choices.feedback: Product line launching! Your signature hot sauce and salad dressing in local stores. People can enjoy your food at home. Brand building!

glossary_terms.definition: The ratio of how much ingredients cost versus menu price. Most restaurants target 25-35% food cost. If ingredients cost 10 MC and you charge 30 MC, that's 33% food cost.
glossary_terms.example: A burger costs 8 MC in ingredients. At 30% food cost target, you should charge around 27 MC to customers.

glossary_terms.definition: Total wages paid to employees as percentage of revenue. Restaurants typically target 25-35% labor cost. Too low means poor service, too high means no profit.
glossary_terms.example: If weekly revenue is 1000 MC and you pay 300 MC in wages, that's 30% labor cost - right in the target range.

glossary_terms.definition: Restaurant industry term for the number of customers served. 'We did 80 covers tonight' means 80 diners were served.
glossary_terms.example: Saturday night did 100 covers at 30 MC average check = 3000 MC revenue for that night.

glossary_terms.definition: In restaurants, 85% of complaints are about service, only 15% about food. Service quality often matters more than food quality for customer satisfaction.
glossary_terms.example: Amazing food with rude service = bad review. Good food with excellent service = loyal customer.
